sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface expression confirmed by flow cytometry (Myc-tag detected on intact cells). Receptor function (adenosine signalling) not explicitly assayed in the cited clips.
sites.rationale: L8 establishes that a Myc tag inserted into an extracellular region of full-length hA1R is tolerated and surface-displayed, but the paper specifies only 'extracellular region' without naming ECL1, ECL2, ECL3, or the N-terminus. ADORA1 has four extracellular spans (N-term 1–9, ECL1 69–81, ECL2 147–179, ECL3 257–267); choosing among them would require inventing a position not stated in the ledger, which is forbidden. The site is therefore reported at region level with insert_after_residue = null. Ranked below the N-terminal site because the junction is unpinned. A short Myc-tag sequence was engineered onto the extracellular region of wild-type full-length human A1R to confirm cell-surface expression; surface display was validated by flow cytometry in anti-Lewis Y CAR T cells (L9 corroborates). The paper does not name a specific extracellular loop or residue.

sources.claim: Due to the lack of reliable flow cytometry antibodies for the hA 1 R, a short Myc-tag sequence was engineered onto the extracellular region of the wild-type hA 1 R to confirm protein expression on the cell surface (Supplementary Fig. 2 C, and Supplementary Table 1 ).

sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface expression confirmed by NanoBiT luminescence complementation (LgBiT added extracellularly to intact cells); agonist-stimulated receptor internalisation also monitored with the tagged construct, showing the receptor remains functional for trafficking. Ligand-binding or G-protein coupling not explicitly quantified in the cited clip.
sites.rationale: ADORA1 is a GPCR with no signal peptide; the topology landmarks place residues 1–9 extracellular and TM1 beginning at residue 10 (A), giving 9 residues of buffer between a prepended tag and the first TM helix — well above the ≥3-residue minimum. The N-terminus is the only extracellular terminus of a GPCR, so 'N-terminus' unambiguously maps to insert_after_residue = 0 (prepend before M1). Python confirms residue_after = 'M' (position 1). Three independent papers (PMC6974774, PMC4513639, PMC7116137/Sinobiological) all place tags at this same junction, providing convergent evidence. Full-length human A1AR with HiBiT fused to its N-terminus expressed in HEK293 cells; NanoBiT complementation with exogenous LgBiT used to monitor receptor presence at the cell surface of living cells. The same paper also reports a prior NanoLuc–A1AR N-terminal fusion (replaced by HiBiT), confirming the N-terminus tolerates large protein fusions. L7 (PMC4513639) independently reports N-terminal FLAG and SF-TAP tags on the full-length receptor; L5 (PMC7116137/Sinobiological) reports a commercial N-terminal FLAG construct — both corroborate this junction.

sources.claim: NanoBiT has provided a platform for assessing protein–protein interactions in vitro in real time. 24 , 30 – 32 Here, we have used the NanoBiT complementation technology to monitor the presence of the human A 1 receptor, tagged on its N-terminus with HiBiT, at the cell surface of living cells following addition of purified LgBiT ( Fig. 1a ).

literature_notes: L2, L3, L4 (PMC6974774) describe the same HiBiT–A1AR construct as L1 and were used to confirm the N-terminal junction; they do not add a new site. L7 (PMC4513639) independently reports N-terminal FLAG and SF-TAP tags on the full-length receptor — same junction (position 0) as Site 1, so no additional site is created, but it raises confidence in the N-terminal position. L5 (PMC7116137) references a Sinobiological commercial plasmid with an N-terminal FLAG tag; the position is stated as N-terminal (not unstated), so it is not disqualified on that ground, but since it is a vendor product and the junction is already covered by Site 1 with higher-tier evidence, it is noted here rather than listed as a separate site. L9 (PMC12229354) corroborates L8 (same construct, same paper) and adds no new positional information. The C-terminal eYFP fusion (L6) is placed in other_positions because the C-terminus (residues 291–326) is intracellular per the topology landmarks.

literature_other_positions.note: eYFP fused to the C-terminus of full-length A1AR; the C-terminus (residues 291–326) is intracellular per topology landmarks, so this is not a surface tag site.
